title: Tzadi
hook: the letter of tzaddik, the righteous one

segments.voice: Yesterday, peh, the mouth, and Moses slow of speech. Your line: peh is a mouth. Today, a letter with a whole person in its name.

One short phrase in one verse has kept readers arguing. It's about Noah. In the King James words: "Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations." Just translates the Hebrew tzaddik, righteous. Fine. But why add in his generations? Is the Torah praising him for staying good in a violent age? Or quietly holding back, saying he only looked good next to the people around him? The rabbis heard it both ways, and kept both. Today's letter begins the word they were arguing about.
screen: `NOAH: A JUST MAN.` → `IN HIS GENERATIONS.` → `PRAISE, OR A HEDGE?`

segments.voice: Tzadi makes a ts sound, and it begins tzaddik, a righteous person. Four angles. First, the argument. In the Talmud, one sage says: in his generations, and all the more so had he lived among good people, he would have been greater. Another says: in his generations, but not in others. Rashi puts the second view sharply: next to Abraham, he would have counted for little. Rashi brings both readings side by side and doesn't pick. Second, the word itself. A tzaddik in the Torah is not a statue. Noah is called righteous, and a few chapters later he plants a vineyard and gets drunk. The title doesn't mean flawless. It means a life that leans toward what's right, in a real time and place. Third, the family. Tzaddik shares its root with tzedek, justice, and tzedakah, the giving Jews owe to people in need. In Jewish law tzedakah isn't optional generosity; it's what righteousness looks like with money in its hand. Fourth, the foundation. Proverbs says, in the King James words, "the righteous is an everlasting foundation." Jewish teachers read it as a picture of the tzaddik: someone the world quietly rests on. Not loud, not perfect. Load bearing. So righteousness here isn't a feeling or a reputation. It's measured in acts, done in your own generation, among the people you actually live with, whether or not anyone better is watching.
screen: `TZADI BEGINS TZADDIK.` · `IN HIS GENERATIONS: TWO READINGS.` · `TZEDEK, TZEDAKAH: JUSTICE IN ACTION.` · `A FOUNDATION THE WORLD RESTS ON.` · then, large: `THE RIGHTEOUS IS AN EVERLASTING FOUNDATION.`

segments.voice: Look around your own generation: your street, your office, your family chat. Where is something a little unjust, or a little undone, like a bill a friend can't cover, a coworker taking blame that isn't theirs, a donation you meant to make? Choose one act you could actually do, not a feeling about it, and picture it start to finish. If you pray, you can ask for the nerve.
Tzadi. The letter that begins tzaddik, the righteous one, and shares its root with tzedek and tzedakah. Today's word.
Your line: tzadi for tzaddik. Not flawless, just a life leaning toward what's right. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jews learn tzadi as the letter of tzaddik, the righteous person, and of tzedakah, the giving to people in need that Jewish law treats as an obligation rather than a choice.
